review_notes: I read the whole target file. It has 18 lemmas, and each one uses an identical `norm_num [...]` call. I read the definitions that call unfolds: sharpTaylor, directRational, transformRational, atomicRational, pieceIntCap, atomIntCap, piUpper, lambdaCap, zCap, slopeCap, atomMass, atomBase, pieceBase, densityCap, densityNum, densityDen and massRational. I grepped the PlanarPacking directory for `register_simp_attr` and for macros wrapping `norm_num`, and found neither. The same long unfolding list appears in about 30 other Certificate files. I did not run Lean, so I can't say whether the proposed bundle changes compile time or behaves identically. The `Nat.factorial` entry is a plain unfold lemma that could also unfold other factorials, and the bundle would need to keep that behaviour. I found no loop or competing-rule problem.

findings.declaration: SharpPlanar.coarse_15_13 … coarse_15_30 (repeated ad hoc norm_num unfolding set)
findings.problem: The file has no simp interface for evaluating the certificate definitions. Each of the 18 lemmas passes the same 17-definition unfolding list, plus `Fin.sum_univ_succ` and `Nat.factorial`, to `norm_num` by hand. The same list is repeated in about 30 other Certificate files. The definitions it unfolds are all concrete rational tables or finite sums: `lambdaCap`, `zCap`, `slopeCap`, `atomMass`, `pieceBase`, `atomBase`, `densityNum`, `densityDen`, `densityCap`, `piUpper`, `massRational`, `pieceIntCap`, `atomIntCap`, `directRational`, `transformRational`, `atomicRational` and `sharpTaylor`. Because the set is spelled out at every call site, any new definition on this path has to be added to every call in every file. One missed copy would make `norm_num` leave a goal stuck.
findings.proposed_change: Define the list once in the library. Either register a dedicated simp attribute with `register_simp_attr` (for example `sharp_cert`), tag the definitions to be unfolded with it, and call `norm_num [sharp_cert, Fin.sum_univ_succ, Nat.factorial]`. Or define a local macro or `syntax` that expands to `norm_num [...]` with this list. Each lemma would then be `by sharp_cert_norm`. Keep the bundle as a scoped or opt-in simp set rather than adding the unfoldings to the global `@[simp]` set. These are table-specific definitions, and unfolding them globally would cause unwanted expansion in other files.
findings.benefit: The unfolding list has one source of truth. The 18 lemmas here and the roughly 30 sibling certificate files would each shrink to one short line. Changing a definition on this path, or adding another table, means editing one place. A reader can see at once that every bound is closed by the same evaluation strategy.
